documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed for f/u. Med rec complete. Pt reports no ED visits or hospital stays since last visit. Tobacco use: yes, daily.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u HTN, CAD, COPD, PAD, AAA.

Rough winter for breathing, no infections though. Stairs harder. Same chest tightness with hills, eases with rest. Calves same.
Smoking 1 ppd.

Vitals: BP 159/85, HR 65, SpO2 91% RA.
Exam: barrel chest, diminished BS, prolonged exp. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. HTN/hypertensive heart disease - 159/85. Continue lisinopril, HCTZ, metoprolol.
2. COPD - more symptomatic. Continue olodaterol. Pulm f/u in July.
3. CAD - stable.
4. Tobacco - counseled.

RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Mail-order renewal request
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Mail-order pharmacy requests new 90-day prescriptions: lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metoprolol succ ER 50, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81 (on med list), olodaterol inhaler. Last olodaterol fill was in December. Pended to PCP.

PCP: renewed all x1 year.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Vitals obtained. Med list reviewed, pharmacy confirmed (mail-order). Current smoker. Pt asked for printed after-visit summary.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: breathing worse over the past year.

Short of breath with less and less - now with getting dressed some mornings and any incline. Occasional cough with sputum, not changed in color. No fever. No chest pain at rest.
Asked about the inhaler: he admits he's been using olodaterol only on days he feels bad, not every day - 'figured I'd save it.' Explained again it is a once-a-day maintenance medicine.
Smoking 1 ppd.

Vitals: BP 149/94, HR 67, SpO2 90% RA, T 37.0.
Exam: mild accessory muscle use on talking. Diminished BS bilaterally, prolonged expiration. No crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
1. COPD, progressive dyspnea - pulm f/u already booked 7/24. Continue olodaterol, take it daily. Will defer further changes to pulmonology.
2. HTN - 149/94. Continue current meds.
3. Tobacco - counseled.

RTC after pulm / AWV in September.

documents.body: Do I need to bring anything to the lung doctor on the 24th

documents.title: RE: lung doctor

documents.body: Bring your inhaler and a list of your medicines. Our office sent them your recent notes. They may do breathing tests, so wear something comfortable.

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONARY CLINIC - FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 07/24/2024

Mr. Haskins returns for follow-up of COPD. His shortness of breath has progressed over the past year. He has an occasional productive cough. He is using his olodaterol inhaler as needed rather than daily.
Smoking: one pack a day, continuing; about 40 years of smoking by his account.

Vital signs within normal limits apart from SpO2 88% at rest on room air.
Exam: decreased breath sounds bilaterally, prolonged expiratory phase, mild accessory muscle use.

Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 60%.

Assessment: COPD with progressive dyspnea; continued tobacco use.

Plan: Smoking cessation counseling provided today; this remains the priority. Return to pulmonology clinic in one year.

documents.title: Outside letter received
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pulmonology follow-up note 7/24 received, scanned to chart. FEV1/FVC 60%, resting sat 88% RA. Plan per their note: smoking cessation counseling, return 1 year. Routed to PCP.

orders.order: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening

documents.title: Rooming Note
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Roomed. Vitals x1. Reviewed allergies (NKDA) and meds. Smoking daily, about a pack.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV subsequent.

Pulm note 7/24 reviewed: FEV1/FVC 60%, resting SpO2 88% there, plan smoking cessation, back in a year.
Breathing about the same as June. Still uses the olodaterol on bad days more than every day. Same exertional chest tightness, stable. Calves same.

HRA: independent; slower on stairs. No falls - uses the railing. PHQ-2 1. Alcohol 1-2/wk.
Tobacco: 1 ppd, ~50 pk-yr.

Vitals: BP 168/91, HR 68, SpO2 89% RA, wt 92.3.
Exam: barrel chest, decreased BS, prolonged exp. Heart regular, no murmur. Abd soft, pulsatile mass. Pedal pulses diminished. No edema.

Prevention: LDCT ordered (2023 Lung-RADS 2). FIT kit. Flu/COVID in October. RSV done 2023. Shingrix, PCV20, Tdap 2018 done.

A/P
1. COPD - per pulmonology. Olodaterol.
2. HTN/hypertensive heart disease - 168/91. Continue lisinopril, HCTZ, metoprolol.
3. CAD/HLD - labs today.
4. AAA 4.4 cm (6/2023) - vascular surgery to rescan.
5. Tobacco - counseled. Declines a date.

RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Lab results

documents.body: Lyle - blood counts, kidney tests and cholesterol all fine (LDL 74, creatinine 0.97). No changes.
